Its really, really fun.

But its not perfect. The gameplay is smooth, graphics are fine for what they're going for, the challenge and excitement is there, but classes could use a rebalance. Like another reviewer mentioned here, as of right now you need two classes to make this game work - engineer and scout. A gunner class is at least nice to have if you have a third friend who wants to play, but driller is absolutely useless.

To fix this, I'd love to see them vary the gameplay so that driller is useful (maybe make some types of ores only able to reach with driller's drill, or even better, dissolve the classes and let all players choose a handful of tools/weapons they'd like to have and find a way to balance things that way. 

In any case, the game is still very fun as it is, and is definitely worth picking up, I have a feeling my friends and I are going to be playing it for many years to come.

ROCK AND STONE

Not often do I play a multiplayer game and love it as much as the singleplayer games in my library; there's a lot of stuff this game does, and it does it all well.

I describe this game as a mixture of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/550/Left_4_Dead_2/]Left 4 Dead 2[/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/361420/ASTRONEER/]ASTRONEER.[/url] Although it isn't the child of these games, it does take the best bits from both of them - the nice looking aesthetics that ASTRONEER has are present in this game, alongside the encouragement of teamwork (from L4D2) by, not limited to, having a great synergy between the different classes and their functions.

Surrounded by AAA games and corporate developers, it's rare to find such a great indie game, with such great developers. They listen to the feedback from the users, take part in conversations on the subreddit + Discord, and actually PLAY the game! They have an active blog with a forever updating roadmap, showcasing upcoming features and estimated delivery dates. They've got it all.

Exactly what you think

Dwarfs in space, fighting bugs and mining gold. Each mission plays like an intense (or mild depending on the difficulty) cave dive in minecraft or the like, but with space dwarfs. 

One of the few cooperative games where you team does not need to be reminded to work together too. Each character has a job. One that they do well, but are able to do so much better with a little help from a different character class.
